chapters.title: Chapter 5: Comparing Markets Like an Investor

lessons.title: Currencies, Time Zones, and FPI Flows: How Global Markets Move the Nifty

children.text: Look at what happened on Tuesday, 15 September 2026. Brent crude had surged to around $108 a barrel on Middle East tensions. The US 10-year Treasury yield had touched 5% the day before, and markets were braced for a possible US Federal Reserve rate hike. Foreign investors had already pulled ₹13,138 crore out of Indian equities in the first two weeks of the month. That day, the rupee fell 38 paise to close at 95.92 per dollar, and the Nifty 50 dropped 1.19% to 23,118.60, its lowest close in five months. Yet IT stocks rose. Nothing in this story started in India, but every part of it ended in your Zerodha portfolio. This lesson shows you exactly how.

body.text: The Nifty is priced in Mumbai but pushed by a global chain: US yields and the dollar move foreign money, foreign money moves the rupee, and the rupee and oil decide which Indian sectors win or lose. Time zones decide when the shock lands, and domestic SIP money decides how hard it hits.

children.text: Global shocks reach Indian stocks through a chain of cause and effect. Once you learn the links, a confusing day like 15 September 2026 becomes easy to read.

body.caption: How a global shock travels to the Nifty, using 15 September 2026
headers: What it looked like on 15 September 2026

cells: 1. Global trigger
Oil, US interest rates or a major event shifts risk appetite
Brent near $108, US 10-year yield near 5%, Fed decision pending
2. Safe-haven dollar
Higher US yields make dollar assets more attractive and strengthen the dollar
A strong dollar weighed on emerging market currencies
3. FPI flows
Foreign investors sell emerging market shares, including Indian large caps
₹13,138 crore of FPI selling in 1 to 11 September
4. The rupee
FPI exits and higher oil import bills raise dollar demand, weakening the rupee
Rupee fell 38 paise to 95.92
5. Sector rotation
Importers and rate-sensitive stocks fall; exporters earning in dollars hold up or gain
Realty and metals fell most; IT stocks rose
6. The index
The Nifty reflects the net effect
Nifty down 1.19% to a five-month low

markDefs.definition: Foreign Portfolio Investors. Overseas funds and institutions registered with SEBI that buy listed Indian shares and bonds. NSDL publishes their daily net investment data.

children.text: are the fastest-moving money in Indian markets. They compare India with every other market in the world, every day. 2026 was a brutal year for foreign flows: FPIs sold Indian equities for four straight months from March to June, briefly returned as buyers in July and August, and turned sellers again in September. Their share of Indian companies has been shrinking for three years.

body.title: FPI selling in dollars
body.prompt: FPIs pulled ₹2.37 lakh crore out of Indian equities in 2026 up to 11 September. Assuming an average exchange rate of 95 rupees per dollar, how much is that in $ billion? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: ₹2.37 lakh crore = ₹2.37 trillion. Divide by 95: 2.37 ÷ 95 = 0.02495 trillion dollars, or about $24.9 billion. Every one of those dollars had to be bought in the currency market, which is a big reason the rupee spent much of 2026 near record lows.

body.text: You will often see two different numbers for foreign selling. NSDL's FPI data, used in this lesson, counts FPI investments including primary market deals such as IPOs and block placements. The "FII" figures that exchanges publish each evening are provisional cash market numbers and can be much larger or smaller. In 2026, one exchange-based tally put foreign selling at about ₹3.40 lakh crore, far above NSDL's ₹2.37 lakh crore. Always check which source a headline uses.

children.text: A decade ago, heavy FPI selling on this scale might have triggered a far deeper crash. Today, Indian households investing through SIPs, along with mutual funds, insurers and pension funds, absorb much of it. This is the single biggest structural change in how global markets affect the Nifty. Foreign money still decides the direction on many days, but domestic money now decides how far the market falls.

columns.label: Foreign Portfolio Investors
points: Net sellers of ₹2.37 lakh crore in 2026 till 11 September
Ownership of NSE-listed companies at a 17-year low of 15.8%
React to US yields, the dollar, oil and other markets
Measure returns in dollars, so a weak rupee hurts them

columns.label: Domestic institutions and SIP investors
points: DIIs bought a net ₹5.13 lakh crore of equities in 2026 till 7 August
Mutual fund ownership at a record 11.6% of NSE-listed companies
Monthly SIP inflows hit a record ₹32,297 crore in August 2026
Invest in rupees on a fixed schedule, largely regardless of global news

body.title: The power of SIPs
body.prompt: Monthly SIP inflows reached ₹32,297 crore in August 2026. If that pace continued for 12 months, how much would SIPs bring in over a year, in ₹ lakh crore? Round to two decimal places.
body.explanation: ₹32,297 crore × 12 = ₹3,87,564 crore. Since ₹1 lakh crore = ₹1,00,000 crore, that is ₹3.88 lakh crore a year. That alone is larger than the ₹2.37 lakh crore FPIs withdrew in the first eight and a half months of 2026. Not all SIP money goes into large caps, but the scale shows why domestic investors can now cushion foreign selling.

body.text: A shock absorber is not a force field. Record SIP inflows and ₹5.13 lakh crore of DII buying did not stop the Nifty from falling to a five-month low on 15 September 2026. Domestic flows reduce the damage from foreign selling, but they do not guarantee that prices go up. If you invest through SIPs, the point is to keep investing through these phases, not to expect them never to happen.

markDefs.definition: The US Dollar Index. A measure of the dollar's value against a basket of major currencies, including the euro, yen and pound. A rising DXY usually means pressure on emerging market currencies like the rupee.

children.text: The rupee and foreign flows feed each other. When FPIs sell, they convert rupees into dollars, which weakens the rupee. A weaker rupee then cuts the dollar value of their remaining Indian holdings, which can push them to sell more. India's oil import bill adds to the pressure whenever crude prices spike, and a strong

makes it worse. The RBI steps in with its reserves, which stood at a record $785.7 billion in the week ended 4 September 2026, to slow sharp falls, but it cannot reverse a trend driven by oil and global flows.

body.title: The foreign investor's double hit
body.prompt: Illustrative figures: over a month, the Nifty 50 falls 5% in rupee terms and the rupee weakens 4% against the dollar. Using (1 + Nifty return) × (1 + currency change) − 1, what is the return for a US-based FPI in dollar terms? Enter a negative number, rounded to one decimal place.
body.explanation: Dollar return = (1 − 0.05) × (1 − 0.04) − 1 = 0.95 × 0.96 − 1 = 0.912 − 1 = −8.8%. An Indian investor loses 5%, but the foreign investor loses 8.8%. This is why FPIs often sell harder when the rupee is falling: they are fighting two losses at once.

body.title: Read the rupee day
body.question: On a day when the rupee falls sharply and Brent crude jumps, which of these Nifty stocks is most likely to hold up or rise?
body.explanation: Infosys earns most of its revenue in dollars and pays most of its costs in rupees, so a weaker rupee lifts its rupee profits. Oil marketing companies and airlines face higher dollar costs for crude and fuel. Real estate is rate-sensitive and tends to fall when oil and bond yields rise. This is exactly why IT stocks rose while the Nifty fell on 15 September 2026.

children.text: Link 3: Time Zones Decide When the Shock Lands

markDefs.definition: When a stock or index opens well above or below its previous close, because news arrived while the market was shut. Stop-loss orders cannot protect you from the gap itself.

children.text: Most major global news arrives while NSE is closed. US data, Fed decisions and US company results land in the Indian evening or at night. By the time the Nifty opens at 9:15 am, GIFT Nifty, Tokyo, Seoul and Hong Kong have already priced it in. That is why Indian stocks so often move in
rather than steady moves through the day. GIFT Nifty itself has become a serious market, with record monthly turnover of $129.80 billion in March 2026.

body.title: Convert the Fed's clock
body.textWithBlank: The US Federal Reserve releases its policy decision at 2:00 pm Eastern Time. During US daylight saving time, when IST is 9 hours 30 minutes ahead, that is ___ IST.
body.explanation: 2:00 pm plus 9 hours 30 minutes is 11:30 pm IST. After US clocks go back on 1 November 2026, the gap becomes 10 hours 30 minutes and Fed decisions arrive at 12:30 am IST. Either way, Indian investors can only react through GIFT Nifty until NSE opens the next morning.

body.text: Oil deserves its own place on your watchlist. India imports most of the crude oil it uses, so every sustained jump in Brent widens the trade deficit, raises inflation risk, weakens the rupee and makes foreign investors more nervous. On 15 September 2026, Brent near $108 was the first domino in the entire chain.

body.title: The morning after a Fed surprise
body.scenario: At 11:30 pm IST on a Wednesday, the Fed unexpectedly raises interest rates by 0.50 percentage points instead of the expected 0.25. Overnight, the US 10-year yield jumps, the dollar index rises sharply and Brent crude climbs above $110. At 6:30 am IST on Thursday, GIFT Nifty is down 1.8%. You hold a Nifty 50 index fund, TCS, HDFC Bank and a real estate stock, and you run a monthly SIP.
body.prompt: Walk through the transmission chain for Thursday. How is each holding likely to react, what role will FPIs, the rupee and domestic investors play, and what should you do about your SIP?
body.modelAnswer:
The chain:
1. Global trigger: A bigger-than-expected Fed hike raises US yields and strengthens the dollar, making US bonds more attractive than emerging market shares.
2. FPIs: Likely to sell Indian large caps, especially heavily owned names like HDFC Bank.
3. Rupee: FPI selling and a higher oil import bill push the rupee weaker, and the RBI may step in to slow the fall.
4. Index: GIFT Nifty signals a gap-down open of around 1.8%.

Your holdings:
1. Nifty 50 fund: Likely to open lower with the market.
2. TCS: Could hold up better, because a weaker rupee raises the value of its dollar revenue, though global tech mood may limit the benefit.
3. HDFC Bank: Exposed to FPI selling and to the rising-rate environment.
4. Real estate stock: Among the hardest hit, because higher rates and oil-driven inflation fears hurt rate-sensitive sectors.

Domestic investors: SIP and mutual fund inflows are likely to absorb part of the selling, which may limit the fall compared with past episodes, but will not necessarily prevent it.

Your SIP: Continue it. SIPs are designed to buy more units when prices fall. Avoid panic selling at a gap-down open, and review individual holdings based on their businesses, not one night's news.

body.title: Track the chain every week
steps: Check the weekly change in the US 10-year Treasury yield and the US Dollar Index.
Check Brent crude and note whether it is above or below levels that worry Indian markets.
Look at NSDL's FPI data for the week and month, not just one day's exchange figures.
Note USD/INR's weekly move and any news of RBI intervention.
Check AMFI's monthly SIP and equity fund inflow data to judge how strong the domestic cushion is.

Domestic institutional investors such as mutual funds, insurers and pension funds. They bought ₹5.13 lakh crore of equities in 2026 till 7 August.
Monthly money invested through systematic investment plans. A record ₹32,297 crore in August 2026, across 10.01 crore SIP accounts.
The dollar's value against major currencies. A rising DXY usually pressures the rupee and emerging market flows.
An open well above or below the previous close, caused by news that arrived while the market was shut.
When a foreign investor loses both on falling Indian share prices and on a weakening rupee.
When a company earns in the same currency as its costs or debts. IT exporters with dollar revenue benefit from a weaker rupee.

points: Global shocks reach the Nifty through a chain: a trigger like oil or US yields, a stronger dollar, FPI selling, a weaker rupee, sector rotation and finally the index.
FPIs sold ₹2.37 lakh crore of Indian equities in 2026 till 11 September, and their ownership of NSE-listed companies fell to a 17-year low of 15.8%.
Domestic investors are now the shock absorber: DIIs bought ₹5.13 lakh crore till 7 August 2026, and SIP inflows hit a record ₹32,297 crore in August.
A weaker rupee gives foreign investors a double hit, but helps dollar earners like IT and pharma exporters while hurting importers and oil-sensitive sectors.
Most global news lands while NSE is closed, so the Nifty reacts through GIFT Nifty and gap openings. A Fed decision at 2:00 pm Eastern arrives at 11:30 pm IST in summer.
Oil is the first domino for India. On 15 September 2026, Brent near $108, US yields near 5% and FPI selling combined to push the Nifty to a five-month low and the rupee to 95.92.
